presentation.guidance: Topic architecture opens with problem-domain analytical prose covering trigger, current technical situation, and cost of unresolved uncertainty — without stating the adopted architecture direction, mixing boundaries, module layout, or feature-level outcomes.

allowed.carrier: Causal analytical prose (trigger → current situation → cost of unresolved uncertainty)
allowed.when: Single causal architecture-pressure narrative; not ≥2 column-aligned items.

forbidden: Named adopted architecture direction and direction-success criteria tables (belongs in AD)
Scope or exclusion tables (belongs in BD)
Module or capability-domain partition tables (belongs in SH)
Feature-milestone dependency diagrams (belongs in FD)
Decision comparison or decision-outcome inventory tables (belongs in KD)
Open-question / pending-item tracking tables (belongs in OQ)
Before/after feature outcome tables (feature-solution granularity, out of scope)

required: States why architecture shaping happens now and what the current technical situation is
States the cost of leaving architecture uncertainty unresolved without naming the adopted direction
forbidden: Opening paragraphs that lead with file:line or repository path inventories
Checkbox steps, Run commands, feature task breakdowns, or acceptance criteria

presentation.guidance: States the named topic-level architecture direction, high-level realization actions, and observable direction-success criteria at milestone granularity — without problem-trigger narrative, scope tables, module layout, or feature-level outcomes.

allowed.carrier: Direction prose plus optional criteria table (named direction → high-level actions → observable success criteria)
allowed.when: Named topic direction plus actions and/or success criteria.

forbidden: Repeating CTX trigger narrative without direction semantics
Scope or exclusion tables (belongs in BD)
Module or capability-domain partition tables (belongs in SH)
Feature-milestone dependency diagrams (belongs in FD)
Decision comparison or decision-outcome inventory tables (belongs in KD)
Open-question / pending-item tracking tables (belongs in OQ)
Before/after feature outcome tables (feature-solution granularity, out of scope)

required: Names an observable topic-level architecture direction without file-level, interface-level, or task-level detail
States high-level realization actions and/or generic observable criteria that show the direction holds
forbidden: Opening paragraphs that lead with file:line or repository path inventories
Checkbox steps, Run commands, feature task breakdowns, or acceptance criteria

presentation.guidance: Boundaries express shaping scope for a multi-feature topic: in-scope capability domains, excluded architecture paths, and cross-feature invariants; each exclusion binds to what it protects.

allowed.carrier: Scope table (capability domain or system | shaping concern in scope)
Exclusion list (excluded architecture path | protected boundary/invariant)

forbidden: Feature change-mapping tables (feature-solution granularity, out of scope)
Module dependency diagrams (belongs in FD)
Trade-off reasoning with adopted/rejected paths (belongs in KD)
Open-assumption tracking (belongs in OQ)

required: Scope, exclusions, and invariants are distinguishable and non-contradictory
Each exclusion identifies the boundary or invariant it protects
forbidden: Repeating CTX trigger narrative without boundary semantics
Single-feature solution scope framed as topic architecture

presentation.guidance: Prefer Mermaid architecture structure diagrams (e.g. C4; UML component/package/deployment; layered structure). Choose the kind that best fits the facts. Prefer one coarse diagram; add finer structure diagrams only when facts remain unconsumed. Carrier priority: diagram > table > analytical prose. Use a table only when facts cannot support nodes/edges.

allowed.when: Structure/topology readable as nodes and edges.
≥2 elements sharing columns; facts cannot support a diagram.
Brief non-structural notes; not matrix or diagram.

forbidden: Prose or lists as the primary carrier of structure (no real diagram)
Structure table before its diagram
Interaction or execution-detail diagrams (e.g. sequence, request-path)
Implementation-structure inventories (class attribute/method lists, table-level ER)

required: Named structure elements with responsibilities and dependencies (on diagram or fallback table)
Each element's link to existing assets is clear (new or extends-existing)
forbidden: Placeholder element names
Restating diagram nodes or edges

presentation.guidance: Prefer Mermaid feature-dependency diagrams (e.g. milestone dependency graph or flowchart). Carrier priority: diagram > table > analytical prose. Use a table only when facts cannot support milestone nodes/edges.

allowed.when: Milestone dependency readable as nodes and edges.
≥2 milestones sharing columns; facts cannot support a diagram.
Brief dependency notes; not matrix or diagram.

forbidden: Module call chains or request paths
Prose or lists as the primary carrier of dependency (no real diagram)
Dependency table before its diagram

required: Named milestone nodes with depends-on and anchors (on diagram or fallback table)
Future feature-cycle entry points remain visible
forbidden: Placeholder milestone names
Restating diagram nodes or edges

presentation.guidance: When multiple architecture paths were genuinely considered at topic level, a comparison structure carries trade-off semantics; single-path decisions may use analytical prose.

allowed.carrier: Architecture path comparison table (path | conclusion | trade-off rationale | reopen condition)
allowed.when: ≥2 genuinely considered paths sharing path|conclusion|rationale|reopen columns.

allowed.carrier: Analytical reasoning prose (single decision, no genuine alternatives)
allowed.when: Single decision; no genuine contrast set.

forbidden: Module layout duplicating SH
Feature dependency graph duplicating FD
Interface field specs or acceptance matrices (feature-solution granularity, out of scope)
Phase tags, Owner, or Timing tables (execution-spec granularity, out of scope)

required: Architecture-level trade-off reasoning beyond stakeholder authorization alone
Rejected alternatives named when genuinely considered
Reopen or evolution conditions stated when reversibility matters
forbidden: Selected direction rationale consisting solely of authorization references
Repeating BD exclusion list without decision semantics
Feature implementation tactics or design patterns at feature-solution granularity

presentation.guidance: Open items carry topic-level tracking semantics: assumption or risk, related architecture gap, and whether the next feature cycle is blocked.

allowed.carrier: Open-item tracking table (item | related gap | blocks-next-cycle or non-blocking | closure condition)

forbidden: Run commands, test file paths, or checkbox steps
Closed decisions restated from KD
Acceptance or verification matrices (feature-solution granularity, out of scope)
blocks-plan labels (feature-cycle disposition, out of scope)

required: blocks-next-cycle or non-blocking label on each item
Closure condition or resolution path when status is non-blocking
forbidden: Items that only repeat SH/FD/KD content without unresolved assumptions
Feature-level verification gaps without topic-level architecture impact
